title: The impact on mental well-being of the urban and physical environment: an assessment of the evidence
review_question: To assess the impact of the urban and physical environment on mental well-being by reviewing health, social sciences, and architectural research, and to develop a preliminary conceptual model.
inclusion_exclusion_criteria: Papers limited to English language and humans. Publications searched manually for relevance. Excluded if not principally about the impact of the residential built environment on mental health.

synthesis_conclusions: The urban and physical environment impacts mental well-being through five key domains: control over internal housing, quality of housing design and maintenance, presence of valued 'escape facilities', crime and fear of crime, and social participation.
These domains are confounded by socio-economic and demographic factors and interact with cultural factors and housing type.
A holistic and systematic approach is needed for needs assessment and designing effective interventions for mental well-being promotion.
The preliminary model developed aims to pull together all aspects of the interface between the urban and physical environment and mental well-being.
evidence_gaps: The developed model of five key domains needs to be validated in an empirical framework to establish the strength of relation between each domain and mental well-being.
Lack of good, methodologically sound studies on housing quality and mental health.
Lack of research on the extent to which natural and artificial light in the home influence mental health.
Good research evidence on health gains from housing investment and specific improvements (e.g., central heating, major refurbishment) is lacking.
